device.description: 12-bit 100 kHz sampling ADC, +/-10 V input, 12-bit or byte-wide parallel bus with R/C, BYTE and BUSY
device.note: ads7804.pdf (SBAS019A) p.2-3 specifications (VDIG 4.75-5.25 V, binary twos complement), p.4 Table I pin assignments, p.5 Table II control line functions, starting a conversion, p.6 reading data, Table III codes, Table IV conversion timing, Figure 2 bit locations vs BYTE, p.7 Figures 3-5

pages: p.2-3 (specifications: VDIG 4.75-5.25 V, VIH to VD + 0.3 V, binary twos complement, bus access / relinquish 83 ns), p.4 (pin configuration, Table I), p.5 (Table II, starting a conversion: CS and R/C low 40 ns), p.6 (reading data: outputs active with R/C high and CS low; Table III codes; Table IV: t4 BUSY low 8 us max, t7 conversion 8 us max, t9 83 ns, t14 83 ns; Figure 2 bit locations for BYTE low/high), p.7 (Figures 3-5)
notModeled: analog input (+/-10 V), internal/external reference and CAP: the result is always the 0 V code 000h (twos complement)

pins 19-22 (all named DZ): LOW with BYTE low, bits 7..4 (pin 19 = bit 7 ... pin 22 = bit 4) with BYTE high; four pins with the same name cannot be bus data pins, so they are never driven and the BYTE-high read models only pins 6-18 (pins 6-9 = bits 3..0, pins 10-13 LOW, pins 15-18 = bits 11..8)

conversion start: the datasheet starts a conversion when CS and R/C are both low (internally ORed, whichever falls last, BUSY high); the model starts one on every R/C falling edge and ignores a start by CS falling while R/C is low; holding both low past the end of conversion (which starts another) is not modeled

reading the previous result during a conversion (valid up to 16 us after the start) and data invalid from then until BUSY rises: the model always outputs the constant 0 V code while R/C is high and CS is low
BUSY delays t3 (65 ns), t5, t10 and the 2 us acquisition time; convert pulse width 40 ns-6 us
variants: single-device datasheet (ADS7804 U / UB grades differ in accuracy only); pin-compatible with the 16-bit ADS7805.
